provenance.description: Deterministic synthetic delay model; no network measurement

assumptions: The server is an ideal reference within this controlled simulation
Clocks have equal rates and a constant server-minus-client offset
Forward and reverse delays are fixed configured values, not Internet observations
Server processing time is known and constant
No packet loss, jitter, oscillator drift, or clock correction is modeled
Symmetric delay introduces no offset-estimation bias under these assumptions
Actual public NTP exchanges do not reveal true clock offset or true one-way delays

data.conclusion: Symmetric delay cancels from the offset estimate in this ideal model; RTT is separate

provenance.description: Deterministic virtual clock step model; no OS synchronization or network measurement

assumptions: The reference/server clock is ideal within this controlled simulation
Client and reference clocks have equal rates and constant offset during the exchange
One-way delays and server processing are fixed configured values, not observed Internet delays
No packet loss, jitter, or oscillator drift is modeled
One instantaneous step changes only virtual client time after the modeled exchange
Before and after correction share the same reference instant; sequence orders the step
Clock offset is a time difference; drift is a rate difference and is not estimated
Live NTP does not reveal known true offset or individual one-way delays
This educational step is not full NTP clock discipline or operating-system synchronization

explanation: The virtual client starts ahead of the reference by its configured initial error
The delay model supplies T1/T4 from this virtual client and T2/T3 from the reference
The shared four-timestamp calculation estimates reference minus client time
Add that estimated offset to virtual time: positive advances it, negative steps it backward
Symmetric delay permits zero residual in the ideal model; asymmetric bias can remain or introduce error
Residual client error and offset-estimation error have different definitions, even when equal here
Only virtual time changes; no oscillator drift is inferred and the host OS clock is unchanged
data.conclusion: The virtual client matches the ideal reference after the modeled symmetric-delay correction
